summary: Iteration 17 (link properties & projects to users via partner email) tested end-to-end. Backend 16/16 pytest green in /app/backend/tests/test_iteration17_linking.py. Frontend verified via Playwright for both admin (Add Property dialog partner rows now have name+email+pct inputs, people datalist autofills email when a known name is typed) and partner user (Shared badge rendered, 'My equity (40%)' = $160,000, no edit/delete buttons, no access to PUT/DELETE). All review-request items pass: (1) property partner email persisted and lowercased server-side at POST /api/properties and PUT /api/properties/{id}; (2) GET /api/properties for partner returns the shared property with shared:true; partner PUT/DELETE return 404 (owner-only via user_id query); (3) GET /api/dashboard for partner returns properties.equity reflecting the 40% share (160000 of 400000) and projects.list contains the linked project with shared:true, my_percentage=40, my_equity=400000 (40% of 1M land_cost); (4) partner can add own contribution under their own partner name (200) but 403 when posting under another partner name; project PUT/DELETE blocked with 403 for non-owner; (5) unlinking (admin PUT with partner email removed) immediately removes the property from the partner's GET /api/properties list; (6) non-admin GET /api/people returns 403 — datalist silently empty for them which is correct. Owner regression unchanged: admin dashboard 200, admin sees property with shared:false, MAISON 7 untouched (not modified).

issues: Accessibility warning in console: 'Missing Description or aria-describedby for DialogContent'. Non-blocking but recommend adding DialogDescription to Add/Edit Property dialog for a11y compliance.

action_items: Optional: add DialogDescription to Add Property dialog to clear accessibility console warning.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py list_properties and _dashboard_data both filter by {$or: [user_id, partners.email]} — this will match the SAME doc twice if an owner also happens to be in their own partners list by email. For current data this is fine (user_id==owner, so the OR branch 'partners.email' only fires when NOT owner) but relying on this is subtle; prefer an explicit elemMatch or defensive de-dup by _id in Python.

In list_projects/_dashboard_data the 'my_partner' resolution falls back to name match if email missing — case-sensitive on name but case-insensitive on email. Standardize (lowercase both) to avoid confusion when a partner's name on project differs by casing from user.name.

Property POST/PUT lowercases partner emails but does NOT validate email format or dedupe duplicate emails in partners array — a typo like 'yash.sojitra34@gmai.com' would silently never link. Consider pydantic EmailStr for partner.email.
